# MarginMail

> MarginMail is a native Mac email app for Gmail and Google Workspace, with a calendar and a personal CRM built in. It notes what needs you, keeps your calendar beside your inbox, and gives everyone you write to a page. AI is optional: Apple Intelligence on your Mac, or your own Claude if you opt in, only on click (that conversation goes to Anthropic under your own plan). There is no MarginMail server for your mail, no analytics, and AI never sends. It is in beta and free during the beta.

Key facts:
- Platform: macOS 26 or later, native SwiftUI app. iPhone companion app later.
- Accounts: Gmail and Google Workspace, multiple accounts in one unified inbox. iCloud and other providers later.
- Price: free during the beta. Pricing not yet announced.
- Privacy: MarginMail talks directly to Google from the Mac. No MarginMail server holds mail, credentials or usage data. No analytics. No read receipts or open tracking.
- AI: optional. Tier 1 rules (no AI), Tier 2 Apple on-device (Request notes), Tier 3 the user's own Claude, signed in on the Mac, only on click (Write it, What's been decided); only that one conversation goes to Anthropic, under the user's own plan. AI never sends email.
- Shipped features: Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests) shown in the reply bar; the Margins stack (drag right for Done, left for Later; "Why this?" on every card; calm scenes when empty); live words (dates, people, files and promises become actions as you type, rules only); Write it (drafts from your notes and the thread, flags anything new); What's been decided (long-thread summary); in-window composer (docked, floating, expanded); Split view (inbox, message and today's calendar side by side; click a name for the person's page); calendar built in (unanswered invites marked, accept with A/M/D, answering files the email, Needs your answer list, find a time with holds); People and Companies, a private personal CRM (a page per person with conversations, meetings, notes, tasks that close themselves and local time; who's waiting on you; companies by domain; stored in the user's own Google account); menu bar agenda with Join; notifications per account (everything, needs you + VIPs, or nothing; quiet hours, Focus filters); Done instead of Archive; typing under 16 ms per key.
- Not for: Windows, Android, Microsoft 365 or iCloud-only users (yet), shared team inboxes, open tracking.
- Contact: hello@marginmail.ai

## Home (https://marginmail.ai/)

### What is MarginMail?

MarginMail is a native Mac email app for Gmail and Google Workspace, with a calendar and a personal CRM built in. It notes what needs you (follow-ups, meeting invites and requests), helps you find a meeting time as you type, and gives everyone you write to a page. Its AI is optional: Apple Intelligence on your Mac, or your own Claude when you click, never a MarginMail server, and it never sends email for you.

### What the margin is for

The margin is where the work gets clear. Every good page of notes has one. It’s where you find time in a full day. Where you keep the facts worth remembering. Where you skim to see what was decided and what still needs you. Where you underline what matters, circle the ask, and make the call. MarginMail brings that to your mail. It finds the time, keeps your people close, marks what needs you, and turns a chaotic day into a short, ordered stack. Then it gets out of the way.

### Follow-up reminders, requests and meeting invites: Only what needs you.

MarginMail writes a short note in the margin when someone's waiting on you, when you're waiting on a reply, or when a meeting invite needs an answer. Open the stack and work through them like cards: drag right for Done, left to send it to the back of the stack.

### Email, calendar and contacts in one Mac window: Your mail, your calendar and your people, side by side.

Open Split view and your whole day is in one window. Read Imogen’s message, and her page is a click away: what you last talked about and the time where she is. Today’s calendar sits beside it. An invite you haven’t answered looks different. Press A, M or D, and its email files itself. No tab to keep open, no app to switch to.

### A private personal CRM, built from your Gmail and calendar: Everyone you write to has a page.

Before a meeting, open their page: what you last talked about, what you promised, who’s waiting on whom, and the time where they are. Tasks close themselves when the reply, the file or the yes arrives. Companies group themselves by email domain. It’s all built from the mail and calendar you already have, and it stays in your own Google account. Nothing to import. Nothing uploaded.

### Google Calendar built in, with Find a time: Find time in the margins of your day.

The full calendar is one click away. Meeting invites you haven’t answered look different, and a Needs your answer list keeps them together, each answered with one key. Need to schedule a meeting? See both calendars side by side, pick a time, and the hold is placed for you.

### Schedule meetings and attach files as you type: Type the plan. MarginMail does the rest.

As you write, dates, people, files and promises become actions. Type “Tuesday with Ava” and both calendars’ free times appear. Type “the pricing deck” and the file is attached. It’s all rules, so it’s instant, private and works with AI off.

### Email summaries and highlighted asks: Skim it. Know what matters.

When someone asks you for something, MarginMail highlights the exact sentence and marks the row in the margin. Every card says why it’s there. On a long thread, What’s been decided sums it up: what’s settled, what’s still open and who’s waiting on whom.

### Private AI email replies you send yourself: A draft from your notes. Sent by you.

Jot a few notes and press Write it. MarginMail drafts the reply from your notes and the thread, right in front of you, and flags anything it added that the thread didn’t have. You read it. You send it.

Write it uses your own Claude, signed in on this Mac, only when you click. Only that conversation goes to Anthropic, under your plan. Request notes use Apple Intelligence, on-device. MarginMail works fully with AI off.

### Private email: no servers, no tracking: Made for the Mac. Made for privacy.

MarginMail is a native Mac app, built from the start to keep your mail yours. There’s no MarginMail server in the middle: we can’t read your mail, and we can’t see how you use the app.

- No usage tracking. No analytics or telemetry in the app, so we can’t see how you use it. This site sets no cookies and doesn’t track you: we count visits anonymously on our own server, with no ads or third parties, and we honor Do Not Track.
- Tracking pixels blocked. Remote images are blocked by default. Load them for one message, or always for a sender you trust. Hidden 1×1 tracking pixels are stripped even when you load images, and the images MarginMail does load are fetched without cookies or referrer.
- No read receipts. MarginMail never adds read receipts or open tracking to the mail you send.
- No MarginMail server. Your mail goes between your Mac and Google, and nowhere else.
- AI that stays with you. Apple Intelligence on your Mac first. Your own Claude only if you opt in, and only when you click. AI never sends.
- Your data, your account. MarginMail’s own data lives in your Google account’s private app folder.

### Inbox zero, with a sunrise: Done feels good here.

Clear the stack and MarginMail shows a calm scene for a moment: a sunrise over the horizon, still water, a beam of light, chosen by the time of day. Small things like that are on purpose.

### FAQ

**What is MarginMail?**
MarginMail is a native Mac email app for Gmail and Google Workspace, with a calendar and a personal CRM built in. It notes what needs you, helps you find meeting times as you type, and gives everyone you write to a page. Its optional AI uses Apple Intelligence on your Mac or your own Claude, and never sends email.

**Is there a native Gmail app for Mac?**
Google doesn’t make a Gmail app for the Mac; Gmail runs in a browser. MarginMail is a native macOS app built on the Gmail API, so your Gmail and Google Workspace accounts get real Mac windows, notifications and keyboard shortcuts, with your calendar and the people you write to in the same window.

**Does MarginMail store my emails on its servers?**
No. There is no MarginMail server for your mail. MarginMail connects directly to Google from your Mac, so your messages stay with you and Google. MarginMail’s own small settings live in your Google Drive’s hidden app folder. There are no analytics in the app, so we can’t see how you use it.

**Does MarginMail have a built-in personal CRM?**
Yes. Everyone you write to gets a page built from your mail and calendar: past conversations, meetings, notes, tasks and their local time, grouped by company. Tasks close themselves when the reply or file arrives. It stays in your own Google account. Nothing is uploaded to a CRM service, and there’s nothing to import.

**Is MarginMail’s AI private?**
Yes. Request notes use Apple Intelligence on your Mac, so nothing leaves it. If you choose, Write it and What’s been decided use your own Claude, signed in on your Mac, only when you click. Only that one conversation goes to Anthropic, under your own plan. MarginMail never sees your Claude login, uses no API key, and runs no AI server.

**Can I use MarginMail without AI?**
Yes. MarginMail works fully with AI off. Follow-up and meeting notes, live words, the calendar, Find a time, People and Companies all run on plain rules. Turning AI on adds Request notes, which are found on your Mac, and Write it, which drafts replies with your own Claude.

**Can MarginMail’s AI send emails for me?**
No, never. MarginMail’s AI can draft a reply, but only you can send it. Before you do, MarginMail flags anything the draft added that the thread didn’t have, such as a new recipient, a link, a number or a code, and labels which AI wrote it.

**Does MarginMail work with multiple Gmail accounts?**
Yes. You can add several Gmail and Google Workspace accounts and see them in one unified inbox, with your calendars together beside it. MarginMail supports Google accounts today. iCloud and other providers are planned for later, and MarginMail will say so clearly when they arrive.

**Does MarginMail have a calendar?**
Yes. Your Google Calendar sits beside your inbox. Invitations you haven’t answered look different and gather in a Needs your answer list. Press A, M or D to accept, maybe or decline, and the invite’s email files itself. Find a time shows both calendars side by side when Google shares theirs with you, and places the hold.

**Can I see my email and calendar in one window on Mac?**
Yes. MarginMail’s Split view shows your inbox, the message and today’s calendar side by side. Click a name to see that person’s page. Answer invites with A, M or D, and their email files itself. It works with several Google accounts and calendars at once.

**How do follow-up reminders work in MarginMail?**
When you’re waiting on a reply, MarginMail notices and writes a note in the reply bar, like “You asked Ava on Oct 9. No reply in 6 days.” The note joins your Margins stack so you can nudge, mark it Done or send it to the back of the stack. It works on rules, with AI off.

**Does MarginMail use read receipts or tracking pixels?**
No. MarginMail never adds read receipts or open tracking to the mail you send. It also blocks remote images in mail you receive by default, so senders’ tracking pixels don’t load unless you allow images for that sender.

**How much does MarginMail cost?**
MarginMail is free during the beta. Pricing will be announced before the beta ends, well before anything changes for you. Joining the beta only needs your email address, and the only email we’ll send is your invite.

**Is there a MarginMail app for iPhone?**
Not yet. MarginMail starts on the Mac, where your mail, calendar and people share one window. An iPhone companion app is planned for later. Until then, your mail stays in Gmail as usual, so you can keep using Gmail on your phone.

**Is MarginMail the same as the Margin app for iPhone?**
No. MarginMail is our own Apple-native email app for the Mac, built for Gmail and Google Workspace, with an iPhone companion app planned for later. It isn’t affiliated with other apps named Margin. Everything about MarginMail is on marginmail.ai, and the beta is free to join.

**What Mac do I need for MarginMail?**
MarginMail needs macOS 26 or later. Request notes use Apple Intelligence, so they need a Mac where Apple Intelligence is available and turned on. Everything else, including the calendar, follow-up notes, live words and People, works without it.

**When can I join the MarginMail beta?**
Join the list on this page and we’ll email you when your invite is ready. We’re letting people in a few at a time so we can listen closely to each wave. Your email address is all we ask for. This site sets no cookies and doesn’t track you; we only count visits anonymously on our own server.

Every mail app makes different trade-offs. These pages say plainly where each one is the better choice.

### MarginMail is the better choice when

- You use **Gmail or Google Workspace** (one account or several) on a **Mac**.
- You want your **calendar and the people you write to** in the same window as your mail.
- You want **AI that's optional, runs on your Mac or your own Claude, and never sends**.
- You'd rather **no vendor server** sat between you and Google.

### MarginMail isn't the right choice (yet) when

- You need **iCloud, Microsoft 365 or IMAP** accounts.
- You need **Windows, Android or a full iPhone app** today.
- Your **team shares an inbox**.
- You rely on **read receipts or open tracking** (MarginMail never offers them).

## MarginMail vs Airmail: customizable vs calm (https://marginmail.ai/compare/airmail/)

**Short answer:** Airmail is a long-running, highly customizable mail app for Apple devices that supports almost every provider, with Airmail Pro at $49.99 a year in the US. MarginMail is a calm, native Mac app for Gmail and Google Workspace that puts your calendar and the people you write to in the same window, notes what needs you, and keeps AI optional: on-device first, or your own Claude when you click. MarginMail is free during its beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026. Prices in USD.*

### At a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **Airmail** |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free during the beta | Free for one account; Pro $49.99/yr or $7.99/mo (US). Apple notified yearly subscribers of a change from $9.99 to $49.99 (Sept 2026) |
| Platforms | Native Mac (macOS 26+); iPhone companion later | Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, Vision Pro |
| Accounts | Gmail and Google Workspace, several in one unified inbox | Gmail, Workspace, iCloud, Exchange (EWS), Office 365, Outlook, IMAP, POP3 |
| Calendar | Built in: unanswered invites marked, A / M / D, find a time with holds | None built in; send mail to Fantastical or Calendar 5 |
| What needs you | Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests) and the Margins stack | Smart Inbox, rules and actions, snooze, custom swipes |
| People | A page per person; companies by domain | Not a feature |
| AI | Optional: Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude, on click (Write it) | Airmail MCP server: connect Claude, Codex or other MCP clients; runs locally on your Mac |
| AI sends mail | Never | Per-capability permissions you choose |
| Servers | No MarginMail server; Mac ↔ Google | Messages not stored on Airmail servers; push uses Airmail's push service |
| Read receipts | Never offered | Mac plugin |
| Customization | Deliberately few settings | Very deep |

### Where Airmail is the better choice

- You use **iCloud, Exchange, Outlook or IMAP** accounts. MarginMail is Google-only today.
- You want **iPhone, iPad, Watch and Vision Pro** apps now.
- You love **customizing everything**: swipes, toolbars, rules, actions.
- You want an **agent to operate your mail through MCP** from Claude or Codex.

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You want the app to **sort for you**, not offer knobs: notes about what needs you, a short stack, Done.
- You want a **calendar in the same window**, with invites you can answer with one key.
- You want **people pages** built from your mail and meetings.
- You want **AI inside the moment** (a draft from your notes and the thread, right in the composer, with anything new flagged) rather than through an outside agent.

### Who should choose which

**Airmail** for multi-provider power users who like to tune their tools. **MarginMail** for Gmail and Workspace users who want calm, a calendar and their people in one window.

### FAQ

**How much is Airmail Pro in 2026?**
In the US, Airmail's help center lists Pro at $49.99 a year or $7.99 a month (checked Oct 16, 2026). In September 2026 Apple notified yearly subscribers of a change from $9.99 to $49.99 at renewal. Prices vary by country.

**Does Airmail have a calendar?**
No built-in calendar. You can share messages to Fantastical or Calendar 5. MarginMail has a calendar in the same window.

**Does Airmail work with Claude?**
Yes, through the Airmail MCP server, which runs on your Mac and lets Claude or other MCP clients work with your mail. MarginMail uses your own Claude inside the app, only when you click Write it, and AI never sends.

**Which accounts does MarginMail support compared with Airmail?**
MarginMail supports Gmail and Google Workspace today, with iCloud and others later. Airmail supports nearly every provider.

**Is MarginMail free?**
Yes, during the beta. Pricing will be shared before the beta ends.

## MarginMail vs Apple Mail: an Apple Mail alternative for Gmail users (https://marginmail.ai/compare/apple-mail/)

**Short answer:** Apple Mail is free, built into every Mac, works with nearly every provider, and in macOS 27 adds relevance search and style-matched Smart Replies through Apple Intelligence. MarginMail is a native Mac app made for Gmail and Google Workspace that adds what Mail leaves to other apps: a calendar in the same window, a page for every person, and notes about what needs you. Both keep AI private; MarginMail is free during its beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026.*

### At a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **Apple Mail (macOS 27)** |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free during the beta | Free with macOS |
| Platforms | Native Mac (macOS 26+); iPhone companion later | Mac, iPhone, iPad |
| Accounts | Gmail and Google Workspace, several in one unified inbox | iCloud, Gmail, Exchange/Outlook, Yahoo, any IMAP |
| Gmail specifics | Uses the Gmail API: real threads, labels, Done, aliases, signatures from Gmail | Uses IMAP for Gmail |
| What needs you | Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests); the Margins stack with "Why this?" | Categories, Priority Messages, summaries |
| Calendar | Built in: unanswered invites marked, A / M / D, Needs your answer list, find a time with holds | Separate Calendar app; suggestions can create an event from a message |
| People | A page per person (conversations, meetings, tasks, local time); companies by domain | Contacts app |
| AI | Optional. Apple Intelligence on your Mac (Requests); your own Claude on click (Write it, What's been decided) | Apple Intelligence: summaries, Smart Replies in your style, Write with Siri, relevance search |
| Where AI runs | Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude plan only if you opt in, on click (that conversation goes to Anthropic under your account). No MarginMail server. | On device and Apple's Private Cloud Compute |
| AI sends mail | Never | No |
| Live words in compose | Yes: dates, people, files, promises become actions | No |
| Tracking protection | Remote images blocked by default; no read receipts | Protect Mail Activity (hides IP, preloads remote content privately) |

### Where Apple Mail is the better choice

- You use **iCloud, Exchange or IMAP** accounts. MarginMail is Google-only today.
- You want mail on **iPhone and iPad** in the same app now.
- You want something **free forever** and already installed.
- You're happy with a **simple list** and a separate Calendar app.

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You live in **Gmail or Google Workspace** and want an app built on the Gmail API, not IMAP.
- You want your **calendar in the same window**, with invites answered by a single key.
- You want **a page for every person** you write to, with their local time and open tasks.
- You want **notes about what needs you**, like "You asked Ava on Oct 9. No reply in 6 days."
- You want **AI drafts from your notes** (with your own Claude), with anything new flagged, that never send.

### Who should choose which

**Apple Mail** for people with mixed providers who want a free, simple client. **MarginMail** for Gmail and Workspace users on a Mac whose days are mail, meetings and people, and who want them together, privately.

### FAQ

**Is there a better Mac mail app than Apple Mail for Gmail?**
If you use Gmail or Google Workspace, MarginMail is built on the Gmail API and adds a calendar, people pages and notes about what needs you, while staying private. Apple Mail is better if you also need iCloud or Exchange accounts.

**Does Apple Mail have a calendar?**
No. Calendar is a separate app on the Mac. MarginMail has a calendar in the same window as your mail.

**What AI does Apple Mail have in macOS 27?**
Relevance-ranked search, Smart Replies in your style, Write with Siri for drafting, plus categories, Priority Messages and summaries. It runs on device and in Apple's Private Cloud Compute.

**Does MarginMail use Apple Intelligence too?**
Yes. MarginMail uses Apple Intelligence on your Mac to find Requests (someone asked you for something). Nothing leaves the Mac. MarginMail also works fully with AI off.

**Is MarginMail free like Apple Mail?**
MarginMail is free during the beta. Pricing will be shared before the beta ends.

**Which macOS do I need?**
MarginMail needs macOS 26 or later.

## MarginMail vs Canary Mail: two takes on private AI email (https://marginmail.ai/compare/canary/)

**Short answer:** Canary Mail is a cross-platform mail app for every major provider, with on-device prioritization, cloud AI for writing and summaries, and PGP encryption on its top plan, from free to $100 a year. MarginMail is a native Mac app for Gmail and Google Workspace with no MarginMail server, AI on your Mac or through your own Claude, a calendar built in, and people pages. MarginMail never sends read receipts. It's free during its beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026. Prices in USD.*

### At a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **Canary Mail** |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free during the beta | Free; Growth $36/yr; Pro+ $100/yr; lifetime option; no monthly plans |
| Platforms | Native Mac (macOS 26+); iPhone companion later | Mac, iPhone/iPad, Windows, Android |
| Accounts | Gmail and Google Workspace, several in one unified inbox | Gmail, Outlook, iCloud, Exchange, IMAP |
| What needs you | Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests); the Margins stack | AI priority inbox, VIP and Flagged views, Mark as Done |
| Calendar | Built in: unanswered invites marked, A / M / D, find a time with holds | Built in: view events, accept invites, suggest times (Copilot Schedule); not on Android |
| People | A page per person; companies by domain | Not a feature |
| AI | Optional. Apple Intelligence on your Mac (Requests); your own Claude on click (Write it, What's been decided) | Prioritization on device (Free); AI Copilot for writing, summaries and search (Growth, Pro+) |
| Where AI runs | Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude plan only if you opt in, on click (that conversation goes to Anthropic under your account). No MarginMail server. | Prioritization on device; writing and summaries with hosted models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Google and others) |
| AI sends mail | Never | Drafts for review |
| Read receipts | Never | Canary sends its own read receipts (on by default on macOS); blocks incoming trackers |
| Encryption | Gmail's standard TLS | PGP and SecureSend (Pro+) |
| Vendor servers | No MarginMail server; Mac ↔ Google | Mail and credentials on device by default; optional push and Cloud Sync use Canary's servers |

### Where Canary is the better choice

- You need **iCloud, Outlook, Exchange or IMAP** accounts.
- You need **Windows or Android** too.
- You need **PGP or encrypted send** to clients (Pro+), or HIPAA support with a BAA.
- You want a **low yearly price** with no subscription surprises.

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You want AI that **never leaves your Mac** unless it's your own Claude, with no hosted model of the vendor's choosing.
- You **don't want read receipts** sent from your mail, ever.
- You want a **calendar that does more**: unanswered invites marked, one-key answers, holds placed when you pick a time.
- You want **people pages** and **notes about what needs you**.

### Who should choose which

**Canary** for people who need every provider and platform, or encryption. **MarginMail** for Gmail and Workspace users on a Mac who want calm, a calendar and their people together, with privacy you can explain in one sentence: no MarginMail server, no analytics, AI on your terms.

### FAQ

**Does Canary Mail's AI run on device?**
Partly. Canary's privacy policy says prioritization models are created and stored on your device, while writing, summarizing and chat use hosted models from OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, Google and others. MarginMail's Request notes run on your Mac with Apple Intelligence; Write it uses your own Claude.

**Does Canary Mail send read receipts?**
Yes, Canary has its own read receipts, on by default on macOS, and it blocks incoming tracking pixels. MarginMail never sends read receipts.

**Does MarginMail support encryption like Canary?**
MarginMail uses Gmail's standard encrypted connections. It doesn't offer PGP; if you need PGP, Canary's Pro+ plan does.

**Which accounts does MarginMail support?**
Gmail and Google Workspace today; other providers come later.

**Is MarginMail free?**
Yes, during the beta. Pricing will be shared before the beta ends.

## MarginMail vs Gmail on the web: a native Gmail app for Mac (https://marginmail.ai/compare/gmail/)

**Short answer:** Google doesn't make a Gmail app for the Mac; Gmail runs in a browser tab, with free Gemini basics and more AI on Google AI Plus ($9.99/mo) and Pro ($19.99/mo). MarginMail is a native Mac app for the same Gmail and Google Workspace accounts. It keeps your calendar and people in one window, notes what needs you, and runs optional AI on your Mac. MarginMail is free during its beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026. Prices in USD.*

### At a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **Gmail on the web + Gemini** |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free during the beta | Free; Gemini extras with Google AI Plus $9.99/mo, AI Pro $19.99/mo; Workspace from $7/user/mo |
| Mac app | Native (SwiftUI), macOS 26+ | None; browser tab |
| Accounts | Gmail and Google Workspace, several in one unified inbox | One account per tab or account switcher |
| What needs you | Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests); the Margins stack with "Why this?" | Category tabs; AI Inbox with suggested to-dos (paid plans) |
| Calendar | Built in: unanswered invites marked, A / M / D, Needs your answer list, find a time with holds | Calendar side panel; "Help me schedule" for one-on-one meetings |
| People | A page per person (conversations, meetings, tasks, local time); companies by domain | Google Contacts |
| AI drafting | Write it: from your notes, on click, with your own Claude; flags anything new | Help Me Write and Suggested Replies (free) |
| Ask your inbox | What's been decided on long threads | AI Overviews in search, Gemini side panel (paid plans) |
| Where AI runs | Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude plan only if you opt in, on click (that conversation goes to Anthropic under your account). No MarginMail server. | Google's cloud |
| Works with AI off | Yes, fully | Yes; smart features can be turned off |
| Live words in compose | Yes: dates, people, files, promises | No |
| Done, not Archive | Yes | Archive |

### Where Gmail on the web is the better choice

- You want **free**, forever, in **any browser** on any computer.
- You want **Gemini answers across Gmail, Drive and Docs**.
- You're on a **Chromebook, Windows or Linux** machine.
- You rely on Gmail's **search operators** and web-only features every day (MarginMail passes Gmail search operators through too).
- You want to drop a **booking page** into a message.
- You set your **out-of-office reply** often (MarginMail doesn't edit it yet).

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You want a **real Mac app**: native windows, keyboard shortcuts, Dock badge, notifications, no tab to lose.
- You have **several Google accounts** and want them in **one inbox**.
- You want **notes about what needs you** and **people pages**, built from mail and calendar you already have.
- You want **AI that starts on your Mac** and uses your own Claude plan only when you click, not another cloud.

### Who should choose which

**Gmail on the web** if a browser tab suits you and Gemini is part of your Google plan. **MarginMail** if you spend your day in Gmail on a Mac and want it calmer, with your calendar and people beside it.

### FAQ

**Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?**
No. Google offers Gmail on the web and on iPhone and Android, but not a Mac app. MarginMail is a native Mac app for Gmail and Google Workspace.

**Is Gemini in Gmail free?**
Help Me Write, thread summaries and Suggested Replies became free for all users in January 2026. AI Overviews in search, AI Inbox and the Gemini side panel need a Google AI or eligible Workspace plan.

**Does MarginMail change anything in my Gmail account?**
MarginMail uses the Gmail API from your Mac. What you do in MarginMail (Done, labels, replies) shows up in Gmail as usual. MarginMail keeps its own small state in your Google Drive's hidden app folder, not on a MarginMail server.

**Can I use several Gmail accounts in MarginMail?**
Yes. Add several Gmail and Workspace accounts; they share one unified inbox.

**Does Google see what MarginMail does?**
Your mail stays with Google as it always has. MarginMail adds no server of its own. Its optional AI uses Apple Intelligence on your Mac, or your own Claude when you click.

**How much does MarginMail cost?**
MarginMail is free during the beta. Pricing will be shared before the beta ends.

## MarginMail vs HEY: calm email without changing your address (https://marginmail.ai/compare/hey/)

**Short answer:** HEY is an email service from 37signals with its own @hey.com addresses (or your domain hosted at HEY), the Screener, and HEY Calendar, for $99 a year. It isn't a Gmail client. MarginMail is a native Mac app that brings calm to the Gmail and Google Workspace accounts you already have: notes about what needs you, New faces for first-time senders, a calendar and people pages. MarginMail is free during its beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026. Prices in USD.*

### At a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **HEY** |
|---|---|---|
| What it is | A Mac app for your existing Google accounts | An email service with its own addresses and hosting |

| Your address | Keep your Gmail or Workspace address | @hey.com or your domain hosted at HEY; Gmail only by forwarding plus send-as; no import of old mail |
| Platforms | Native Mac (macOS 26+); iPhone companion later | Web, Mac, Windows, Linux, iOS, Android |
| Screening new senders | New faces: welcome first-time senders or mark them Not for me, with notes on who you already know | The Screener (HEY's signature feature) |
| What needs you | Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests); the Margins stack | Imbox, The Feed, Paper Trail, Reply Later, Set Aside |
| Calendar | Built in, two-way with Google Calendar: A / M / D, find a time with holds | HEY Calendar; Google/Apple/Outlook calendars only as read-only subscriptions |

| AI sends mail | Never | Agents get the access you grant (a read-only mode exists) |
| Tracking | Remote images blocked by default; no read receipts | Spy-pixel blocking; no read receipts |
| Servers | No MarginMail server; Mac ↔ Google | HEY hosts your mail (37signals; not SOC 2) |

### Where HEY is the better choice

- You want **a fresh start** with a new address and a whole philosophy of email.
- You want **Windows, Linux, Android or the web**.
- You like **The Feed and Paper Trail** for newsletters and receipts.
- You want **your own agent** working your account through a CLI or MCP.

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You want to **keep your Gmail or Workspace address**, history and Google Calendar.
- You want a **calendar that syncs both ways** with Google, with invites answered by one key.
- You want **people pages** and **notes about what needs you**.
- You want **optional AI built in**: on-device first, your own Claude on click, and it never sends.

### Who should choose which

**HEY** if you're ready to move your address and adopt HEY's way of doing email. **MarginMail** if you want HEY-like calm, including a place for new senders, on the Gmail you already have.

### FAQ

**Can I use HEY with my Gmail address?**
Only by forwarding new Gmail mail into HEY and sending as your Gmail address. HEY says it isn't a Gmail client and can't import old mail. MarginMail works directly with your Gmail and Workspace accounts.

**Does MarginMail have a Screener like HEY?**
Yes, in its own form: New faces. First-time senders wait there, with a note on what MarginMail knows ("You wrote to her in 2024"), and you choose Welcome or Not for me once for all their mail.

**Does HEY Calendar sync with Google Calendar?**
Not two-way. HEY can subscribe to Google, Apple or Outlook calendars read-only. MarginMail's calendar is your Google Calendar.

**Does HEY have AI?**
HEY has no built-in AI. You can connect your own agent through the HEY CLI or MCP server. MarginMail has optional AI inside the app: Apple Intelligence on your Mac and your own Claude on click.

**How much does HEY cost compared with MarginMail?**
HEY for You is $99 a year as of October 2026. MarginMail is free during its beta.

## MarginMail vs Mimestream: two native Gmail apps for Mac (https://marginmail.ai/compare/mimestream/)

**Short answer:** Mimestream and MarginMail are both native Mac apps that talk straight to Gmail with no sync server in between. Mimestream is a fast, focused Gmail client at $49.99 a year, with no calendar view and no AI. MarginMail adds a calendar in the same window, a page for every person you write to, notes about what needs you, and optional AI on your Mac. MarginMail is free during its beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026. Prices in USD.*

### At a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **Mimestream** |
|---|---|---|
| Price | Free during the beta | $49.99/yr or $4.99/mo; 14-day trial; no free plan |
| Mac app | Native (SwiftUI), macOS 26+ | Native, macOS 12+ |
| iPhone | Companion app later | Limited TestFlight beta (iOS 26+) for subscribers |
| Accounts | Gmail and Google Workspace, several in one unified inbox | Gmail and Google Workspace; Outlook, IMAP and JMAP "planned" |
| How it syncs | Directly with Google from your Mac; no MarginMail server | Directly with the Gmail API; data and tokens only on your device |
| Calendar | Built in: split view, unanswered invites marked, A / M / D, find a time with holds | No calendar view; an availability banner beside invites, accept/decline, one-click join |
| What needs you | Margin notes (Follow-ups, Meetings, Requests) and the Margins stack | Gmail categories, labels, filters, snooze |

| AI | Optional: Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude on click | None |

| Live words in compose | Yes (dates, people, files, promises; rules) | Markdown, @mentions, templates |
| Tracking | No read receipts; remote images blocked by default | Tracking Prevention for 75+ trackers |
| Gmail settings in-app (filters, vacation responder) | Partly (aliases, signatures, filters for blocks) | Yes, edits Gmail filters and vacation responder |

### Where Mimestream is the better choice

- You want the **lightest, most Gmail-faithful client** and nothing else. Mimestream mirrors Gmail's labels and categories closely and edits Gmail-side filters and vacation replies.
- You need an **iPhone app now** and you're an eligible subscriber (it's in a limited beta).
- You run **an older macOS** (12 through 15). MarginMail needs macOS 26.
- You want **no AI at all, by design**. (MarginMail also works fully with AI off, but offers it.)

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You want your **calendar in the same window**, not just a banner beside invites.
- You want **notes about what needs you**: "You asked Ava on Oct 9. No reply in 6 days."
- You want a **memory for people**: a page for everyone you write to, with their local time.
- You'd like **optional AI that stays private**: on-device first, or your own Claude, never a vendor server.

### Who should choose which

Pick **Mimestream** for a pure, polished Gmail client. Pick **MarginMail** if your days are mail plus meetings plus people, and you want them in one calm window with the same no-server privacy.

### FAQ

**Does Mimestream have a calendar?**
Not a calendar view. It shows your events in a banner beside an invitation so you can check availability, and lets you accept, decline and join. MarginMail has a full calendar in the same window.

**Are MarginMail and Mimestream both private?**
Both talk directly to Google from your Mac with no sync server in between. MarginMail also runs no analytics in the app. If you turn on AI in MarginMail, it runs on your Mac (Apple Intelligence) or through your own Claude.

**Does Mimestream have AI?**
No AI features are listed on Mimestream's site as of October 2026. MarginMail's AI is optional: Request notes on-device, and Write it with your own Claude.

**Does Mimestream have an iPhone app?**
It's in a limited TestFlight beta for subscribers, requiring iOS 26. MarginMail's iPhone companion comes later.

**Which costs less?**
MarginMail is free during its beta; pricing comes later. Mimestream is $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month.

**Can I use both?**
Yes. Both read the same Gmail account, so you can try MarginMail without leaving Mimestream.

## A Notion Mail alternative for Mac: MarginMail (https://marginmail.ai/compare/notion-mail/)

**Short answer:** Notion Mail closed on September 22, 2026, across web, Mac and iOS; your mail stayed in Gmail. If you want a Mac app for that same Gmail, MarginMail is a native macOS mail app with a calendar built in, a page for every person you write to, and optional AI that runs on your Mac or through your own Claude. It's free during the beta.

*Last checked: October 16, 2026.*

### What happened to Notion Mail

- **Announced** June 25, 2026. **Closed** September 22, 2026, on web, desktop and iOS. It launched in April 2025.
- **Why:** Notion said more than half its users handled email without opening the inbox, and that it was going "all in" on agents to run the inbox.
- **Your mail is safe.** It always lived in Gmail. What lived only in Notion Mail (drafts, scheduled sends, snippets, auto-label instructions, custom views) had to be exported by September 21.
- **Notion's suggestion:** Notion Custom Agents connected to Gmail or Outlook. Those work inside Notion; there's no mail inbox to read in.

If you still want an inbox (a calm one), that's the gap MarginMail fills.

### Notion Mail and MarginMail at a glance

| | **MarginMail** | **Notion Mail** (at closing, Sept 2026) |
|---|---|---|
| Status | In beta, free during the beta | Closed Sept 22, 2026 |
| Platforms | Native Mac app (macOS 26+); iPhone companion later | Was web, Mac and iOS |
| Accounts | Gmail and Google Workspace, several accounts in one unified inbox | Was Gmail (Outlook not supported) |
| Sorting | Margin notes for Follow-ups, Meetings and Requests; the Margins stack (Done / Later); "Why this?" on every card | AI auto-labels and custom views |
| Calendar | Built in: unanswered invites marked, accept with A / M / D, find a time with holds | Separate (Notion Calendar) |
| People | A page for everyone you write to; companies by domain | Not built in |
| Writing help | Live words (rules); Write it with your own Claude, on click | Notion AI drafting |
| Where AI runs | Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude plan only if you opt in, on click (that conversation goes to Anthropic under your account). No MarginMail server. | Notion's cloud |
| AI sends mail by itself | Never | No (drafts) |
| Works with AI off | Yes, fully | AI was central |
| MarginMail/Notion servers hold your mail | No MarginMail server; Mac ↔ Google only | Processed in Notion's service |
| Analytics in the app | None | Standard product analytics |

### Who should choose which

- **Choose Notion Custom Agents** if you liked Notion Mail mostly because you never opened it, and you want an agent to label, archive and draft for you inside your Notion workspace.
- **Choose MarginMail** if you want a real inbox again: one that shows only what needs you, puts your calendar and people beside it, and keeps your mail between you and Google.
- **Neither** if you need Outlook or Windows today.

### Moving from Notion Mail to MarginMail

1. Your Gmail is already intact; there's nothing to import.
2. Join the beta and sign in with Google. Add every Google account you use; they share one inbox.
3. Notion Mail's auto-labels don't carry over. MarginMail doesn't need labels to sort: its notes find what needs you, and the rest can be marked Done.
4. Recreate snippets as MarginMail templates (type `;` in the composer).

### FAQ

**When did Notion Mail shut down?**
September 22, 2026, on web, Mac and iOS. Notion announced it on June 25, 2026.

**Did I lose my email when Notion Mail closed?**
No. Notion Mail was a client for Gmail, so your messages stayed in Gmail. Only data stored inside Notion Mail itself, like drafts, snippets and custom views, had to be exported.

**What's the best Notion Mail alternative for Mac?**
If you want a native Mac app for Gmail with a calendar and people built in, MarginMail is made for that. If you want an agent to work your inbox without an inbox app, Notion's own Custom Agents are the path Notion recommends.

**Does MarginMail use AI like Notion Mail did?**
Yes, but differently. MarginMail works fully with AI off. When you turn AI on, Request notes use Apple Intelligence on your Mac, and Write it uses your own Claude, only when you click (that conversation goes to Anthropic, under your plan). There's no MarginMail server, and AI never sends.

**Does MarginMail work with Notion?**
Not directly today. MarginMail focuses on mail, calendar and people on your Mac.

**How much does MarginMail cost?**
MarginMail is free during the beta. Pricing will be shared before the beta ends.

### Sources

- 9to5Mac, "Notion shutting down its AI-powered email client, including Mac and iOS apps," June 25, 2026: https://9to5mac.com/2026/06/25/notion-shutting-down-its-ai-powered-email-client-including-mac-and-ios-apps/ (read Oct 16, 2026)
- Toolradar, "Notion Mail is shutting down: alternatives," updated Oct 16, 2026: https://toolradar.com/blog/notion-mail-shutting-down-alternatives

**Short answer:** The new Outlook for Mac is free, keeps mail and calendar in one app, supports almost every provider, and adds Copilot with Microsoft 365 plans from $9.99 a month. MarginMail is a native Mac app for Gmail and Google Workspace that also keeps mail and calendar together, adds people pages and notes about what needs you, and keeps AI optional: Apple Intelligence on your Mac, or your own Claude on click. | | **MarginMail** | **Outlook for Mac (new Outlook)** |

### Where Outlook is the better choice

- Your company runs on **Microsoft 365 or Exchange**. MarginMail doesn't support Microsoft accounts yet.
- You need **Windows, web or Android** too.
- You want **Copilot** across Word, Excel and Outlook under one subscription.
- You're mixing **many providers** in one app.

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You live in **Gmail or Google Workspace** and want a Mac app built for it.
- You want **AI that starts on your Mac** and uses your own Claude only when you click, and **never sends**.
- You want **people pages** and **notes about what needs you**, not just a focused list.
- You want **live words**: type "Tuesday with Ava" and both calendars' free times appear.

**Outlook** for Microsoft 365 workplaces and mixed-provider power users. **MarginMail** for Google Workspace and Gmail people who want Outlook's mail-plus-calendar feel in a calm, private, native Mac app.

### FAQ

**Is Outlook for Mac free?**
Yes. The new Outlook for Mac is free; without a Microsoft 365 subscription it's ad-supported. Copilot features come with Microsoft 365 plans (Personal is $9.99 a month as of October 2026).

**Can I use Outlook for Mac with Gmail?**
Yes, Outlook can add Google accounts. MarginMail is built only for Google accounts and uses the Gmail and Google Calendar APIs directly from your Mac.

**What happened to legacy Outlook for Mac?**
Microsoft retired Exchange Web Services in Exchange Online in October 2026, so legacy Outlook for Mac stops working with Exchange Online; Microsoft says most users have moved to new Outlook.

**Does MarginMail support Microsoft 365?**
Not yet. MarginMail supports Gmail and Google Workspace today; other providers come later.

**Does MarginMail have Copilot-style AI?**
MarginMail's AI is optional and private: Apple Intelligence on your Mac finds requests, and your own Claude writes a draft from your notes when you click Write it (only that conversation goes to Anthropic, under your plan). It never sends.

| Models | Apple on-device; your Claude plan | Claude Haiku 4.5 / Sonnet 4.6 / Opus 4.6 by plan; self-hosted open models for much of the work |
| Where AI runs | Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude plan only if you opt in, on click (that conversation goes to Anthropic under your account). No MarginMail server. | Shortwave's cloud (Google Cloud); sub-processors include OpenAI, Anthropic, Pinecone |
| AI sends mail | Never | Not documented either way |
| Read receipts | Never | Read statuses and link tracking |
| Security attestations | No server to attest; Mac ↔ Google | CASA Tier 2; SOC 2 not claimed |
| Works with AI off | Yes, fully | AI is the core of the product |

### Where Shortwave is the better choice

- You want **the most capable AI agent** in an inbox today: answers across many threads, multi-step tasks, web browsing.
- You want to **connect other tools** (HubSpot, Notion, Slack, Asana, Linear, your own MCP servers).
- You need **Windows, web or Android**.
- Your **team** works in shared threads with comments.

### Where MarginMail is the better choice

- You want AI that **runs on your Mac or through your own Claude plan**, not a vendor's cloud.
- You want an app that's **calm and useful with AI off**, then better with it on.
- You want **people pages** and **live words** that turn "Tuesday with Ava" into free times.
- You want to **see every change AI made**: Write it flags anything new (recipient, link, number) and never sends.
- You'd rather not pay **$30–120 per seat** to try something new.

### Who should choose which

**Shortwave** if you want an AI to do as much of your email as possible and you're comfortable with cloud processing. **MarginMail** if you want help at the right moment, on your terms, with your mail staying between you and Google.

### FAQ

**What AI does Shortwave use?**
Shortwave's pricing page names Claude Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 by plan, and its security page says much of its AI work runs on open-source models on its own hardware. MarginMail uses Apple Intelligence on your Mac and, if you opt in, your own Claude plan, only when you click.

**Is there a Shortwave alternative that keeps AI private?**
MarginMail is designed for that: AI is optional, runs on your Mac first, and never goes through a MarginMail server. It also works fully with AI off.

**Does Shortwave support Outlook?**
Shortwave says Microsoft 365 and Exchange aren't supported. MarginMail also supports Google accounts only today.

**Can I use my own Claude with MarginMail?**
Yes. MarginMail uses the Claude you already have signed in on your Mac, under your own plan; only the conversation you click on goes to Anthropic. It never sees your login and doesn't use an API key.

**How much does Shortwave cost compared with MarginMail?**
Shortwave's paid plans are $30, $45 and $120 per seat a month as of October 2026. MarginMail is free during its beta.

- Your mail stays in Gmail; nothing to import.
- Spark's Gatekeeper → MarginMail's New faces for first-time senders.
- Spark's "Done" → MarginMail's Done (same idea: handled mail leaves).

- You can run both side by side while you try MarginMail.

### FAQ

**Is Spark private?**

**Can Spark's AI send email on its own?**
Spark's Auto-Drafts never send automatically. But Spark CLI's Send permission, added in July 2026, lets an outside agent send without approving each message. MarginMail's AI can never send.

**Does MarginMail work on Windows or iPhone?**
MarginMail is a Mac app. An iPhone companion comes later. There are no plans for Windows.

## The best Gmail apps for Mac in 2026 (https://marginmail.ai/best/gmail-apps-for-mac/)

**Short answer:** Google doesn't make a Gmail app for the Mac, so you choose between native clients and the browser. For a pure native Gmail client, Mimestream. For free and simple, Apple Mail. For every platform and provider, Spark. For the most AI, Superhuman or Shortwave. For mail, calendar and people in one private Mac window, MarginMail (our app, in beta).

*Last checked October 16, 2026. Prices in USD. **Disclosure:** we make MarginMail. It's included, labeled, and held to the same questions as the others.*

### How we judged

Five questions that matter for Gmail on a Mac:
1. **Native?** A real Mac app, or a web view or browser tab.
2. **Gmail-aware?** Built on the Gmail API (labels, threads, aliases) or generic IMAP.
3. **Calendar?** In the same window, or somewhere else.
4. **Where does AI run?** Vendor cloud, Google's cloud, on-device, your own model, or none.
5. **Price** for one person.

### At a glance

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **MarginMail** (ours, beta) | Mail, calendar and people in one private window | Free during the beta | Native SwiftUI on the Gmail API; several Google accounts in one inbox | Built in: A / M / D answers, find a time with holds | Optional: Apple Intelligence on your Mac; your own Claude on click; never sends |
| **Mimestream** | A pure, polished native Gmail client | $49.99/yr or $4.99/mo | Native, Gmail API, no sync server | Invite banner with availability; no calendar view | None |
| **Apple Mail** | Free and simple, any provider | Free | Native, IMAP | Separate Calendar app | Apple Intelligence: summaries, Smart Replies in your style; on-device and Private Cloud Compute |
| **Spark** | Every platform and provider, a free plan, teams | Free; Plus $10/mo; Pro $20/mo | Cross-platform app; Gmail and most providers | Built in | +AI writing and assistant; on-device and/or cloud providers; Auto-Drafts beta |

### The apps

#### MarginMail: best for mail, calendar and people in one private window (ours)
A native Mac email app for Gmail and Google Workspace. It writes short notes about what needs you (follow-ups, meeting invites, requests), turns them into a stack you swipe through beside your calendar, and gives everyone you write to a page. Live words turn "Tuesday with Ava" into both calendars' free times. There's no MarginMail server and no analytics; AI is optional, on your Mac or your own Claude, and never sends.
**Choose it if** you live in Gmail on a Mac and want your day in one window. **Skip it if** you need iCloud or Microsoft accounts, Windows, or an iPhone app today. macOS 26+.

#### Mimestream: best pure native Gmail client
Fast, focused and faithful to Gmail's labels, filters and categories, talking straight to the Gmail API with data only on your device. No calendar view and no AI. iPhone app in a limited TestFlight beta.
**Choose it if** you want Gmail, natively, and nothing else.

#### Apple Mail: best free option
Built into every Mac, works with nearly any provider, and macOS 27 adds relevance search and Smart Replies in your style. Gmail works over IMAP, so labels behave like folders. Calendar is a separate app.
**Choose it if** you mix providers and want free and simple.

#### Spark: best for every platform
Mac, Windows, iPhone, Android; Gmail, iCloud, Outlook and IMAP; Smart Inbox, Gatekeeper and team features. Spark's servers handle Send Later, push and shared mail, and its AI can use cloud providers.
**Choose it if** you need cross-platform and a free plan.

#### Superhuman Mail: best for speed and AI help
Keyboard-first speed with Auto Drafts, Ask AI and a Mail MCP for outside agents. Gmail and Microsoft 365. Cloud-processed, with read statuses.
**Choose it if** maximum AI help is worth $25–40 a month.

#### Shortwave: best AI agent for Gmail
An AI agent that searches across many threads, drafts, schedules and organizes, with Claude models by plan. Gmail only; Microsoft 365 isn't supported.
**Choose it if** you want AI to do as much of your email as possible.

#### Canary Mail: best for encryption on a budget
Every provider and platform, PGP and SecureSend on Pro+, low yearly pricing. Prioritization runs on-device; writing uses hosted models. Sends its own read receipts by default on macOS.
**Choose it if** you need encryption or every provider.

#### Outlook for Mac: best for Microsoft 365 people
Free, mail and calendar together, adds Google accounts, Copilot with Microsoft 365.
**Choose it if** your work runs on Microsoft 365.

#### Gmail in the browser: best free, anywhere
No install, Gemini basics free since January 2026, more with Google AI plans.
**Choose it if** a tab works for you.

### FAQ

**Is there an official Gmail app for Mac?**
No. Google offers Gmail on the web, iPhone and Android, but not as a Mac app. On a Mac you use a browser or a third-party client such as Mimestream, MarginMail, Apple Mail, Spark, Superhuman, Shortwave, Canary or Outlook, each with different trade-offs in price, privacy and features.

**What is the best native Gmail client for Mac?**
Mimestream is the most established native Gmail-only client, built on the Gmail API with no sync server. MarginMail is a newer native Gmail app that adds a calendar, people pages and optional on-device AI; it's in free beta. Apple Mail is native too but uses IMAP.

**Which Mac email app has a built-in calendar for Gmail?**
MarginMail, Spark, Superhuman, Shortwave, Canary and Outlook all include a calendar. MarginMail keeps it in the same window as your mail, with one-key invite answers and a find-a-time view. Mimestream shows only an availability banner on invites; Apple Mail uses the separate Calendar app.

**Which Gmail app for Mac is the most private?**
Apps that talk to Gmail directly from your Mac, with no server of their own, are the most private. Mimestream and MarginMail work this way. MarginMail also runs no analytics and keeps its optional AI on your Mac or your own Claude, and it never sends.

**Is Apple Mail good for Gmail?**
It works, and it's free. Because it uses IMAP, Gmail labels act like folders and some Gmail features don't carry over. If you live in Gmail all day, a Gmail API client such as Mimestream or MarginMail fits Gmail more naturally.

## Email follow-up reminders on Mac: see who hasn’t replied (https://marginmail.ai/guides/email-follow-up-reminders-mac/)

**Short answer:** Gmail doesn't keep a list of sent emails nobody answered. Its Nudges feature brings some back automatically, and browser extensions add "remind me if no reply" to Gmail in Chrome. On a Mac, MarginMail, a native email app for Gmail, notices when you're waiting on someone and writes a note like "You asked Ava on Oct 9. No reply in 6 days," with no AI needed.

*Last checked October 16, 2026.*

### Three ways to track follow-ups

| Approach | How it works | Good for | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Gmail Nudges** | Gmail can suggest older emails to follow up on or reply to, at the top of your inbox (Settings › General › Nudges) | Free, nothing to install | Gmail chooses which emails come back; there's no full "waiting on" list |
| **A browser extension** (for example, Boomerang for Gmail) | Adds "remind me if no reply in N days" to Gmail in your browser | Precise reminders on chosen emails | Works in the browser only; the extension's service handles your mail |
| **A mail app that tracks it for you** (MarginMail on Mac) | Notices who you're waiting on and brings it back as a note and a card | No setup per email; also works for what *others* asked you | MarginMail needs your Mac running to fire reminders on time |

### How follow-ups work in MarginMail

1. **Write and send as usual.** MarginMail keeps track of threads where you asked something and the other person hasn't answered.
2. **A note appears when it's late.** The reply bar shows a Follow-up note in one line: "You asked Ava on Oct 9. No reply in 6 days." Hover for the why and the source message.
3. **Work it from the stack.** Follow-ups join the Margins stack beside your calendar. Reply to nudge, drag right for Done, or left for Later.
4. **Set a specific reminder when you want one.** From the composer or any thread, choose **Remind me if no reply** in a few days. If no one answers, the thread comes back to the top with "No reply yet."
5. **See everyone you're waiting on.** In People, **Waiting on them** lists who owes you a reply, and **Waiting on your reply** lists who you owe. Tasks you add can close themselves when the reply or attachment arrives.

**What it doesn't need:** AI, an extension, or a server. Follow-ups are rules that run on your Mac. With Apple Intelligence on, MarginMail also finds **Requests**, the sentences where someone asked *you* for something, and highlights them word for word.

**Calm by default:** MarginMail shows a few notes a day (5 by default, adjustable from 3 to 7), only when it's sure, and respects quiet hours. "Not useful" teaches it to stop.

### FAQ

**How do I see which of my Gmail emails haven't been replied to?**
Gmail doesn't keep a full list. Its Nudges setting brings back some older emails automatically. On a Mac, MarginMail tracks it for you: follow-up notes show who hasn't replied and for how long, and the People view lists everyone you're waiting on.

**Does Gmail have follow-up reminders?**
Gmail has Nudges, which can suggest emails to follow up on, but it picks them for you and doesn't let you set "remind me if no reply" on a specific email. Extensions and some mail apps add that. MarginMail offers both automatic follow-up notes and a per-thread "Remind me if no reply."

**Is there a follow-up reminder app for Mac that isn't a browser extension?**
Yes. MarginMail is a native Mac email app for Gmail and Google Workspace with follow-up notes and "Remind me if no reply" built in. It runs on your Mac with no extension and no MarginMail server.

**Do follow-up reminders in MarginMail use AI?**
No. Follow-up notes and reminders run on rules on your Mac. AI is optional in MarginMail and adds Request notes, found on-device by Apple Intelligence.

**Does MarginMail track whether people opened my email?**
No. MarginMail never adds read receipts or tracking pixels. It tracks replies, not opens.

- Boomerang for Gmail: https://www.boomeranggmail.com (read Oct 16, 2026)
- MarginMail features: https://marginmail.ai

## Private AI email: what stays on your Mac (https://marginmail.ai/guides/private-ai-email/)

**Short answer:** An AI email app is only as private as the place its AI runs. Most AI mail apps send your messages to their own cloud or to a model provider. The most private setup keeps mail between you and your provider, runs AI on your Mac, and only uses a cloud model you chose, when you ask. MarginMail, a native Mac email app for Gmail, is built that way, and its AI never sends.

*Last checked October 16, 2026. Sources at the end.*

### Where your email goes when an app uses AI

There are five common setups. Ask any mail app which one it uses.

| Setup | Where your mail is processed | Examples (Oct 2026) |
|---|---|---|
| **Vendor cloud** | The app maker's servers, often with OpenAI or Anthropic models behind them | Superhuman (Superhuman's cloud, Anthropic and OpenAI models); Shortwave (its cloud on Google Cloud, Claude models by plan); Spark (on-device and/or Azure OpenAI, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Vertex AI per its policy) |
| **Your mail provider's cloud** | Google's or Microsoft's own AI | Gmail with Gemini; Outlook with Microsoft 365 Copilot |
| **On-device, plus the platform's private cloud** | On your device, with heavier requests in Apple's Private Cloud Compute | Apple Mail with Apple Intelligence |
| **Bring your own model or agent** | A model or agent you connect, under your own account | Missive (your own OpenAI, Anthropic or Gemini key); Airmail and HEY (your own agent through MCP or a CLI) |
| **No AI** | Nowhere | Mimestream |

None of these is wrong. They're trade-offs between capability, convenience and how many companies handle your mail.

### Five questions to ask any AI email app

1. **Does the app maker run a server that stores or processes my mail?** If yes, ask what's kept and for how long.
2. **Which AI model reads my mail, and under whose account?** Yours, the app maker's, or your mail provider's?
3. **Does AI run when I'm not asking?** Background triage means more of your mail is read by a model.
4. **Can the AI send email, or change things, on its own?** Look for "drafts only" and an explicit send step.
5. **Does the app work with AI off?** If not, privacy and usefulness are tied together.

### How MarginMail answers them

MarginMail uses three tiers. Each one says what it is when it appears.

| Tier | What it does | Where it runs | What leaves your Mac |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Rules** | Follow-up and meeting notes, live words (dates, people, files, promises), the calendar, Find a time, People and Companies | Your Mac | Nothing beyond the normal Gmail and Google Calendar requests every mail app makes |
| **2. Apple on-device** | Request notes: finds the sentence where someone asked you for something, highlights it word for word, and says what it's based on | Apple Intelligence on your Mac | Nothing. No account or key is involved |
| **3. Your own Claude** (opt in) | **Write it** drafts a reply from your notes and the thread; **What's been decided** summarizes long threads | The Claude Code you installed on your Mac, signed in to your own Claude plan | Only the conversation you clicked on, sent by your Claude to Anthropic under your account's terms. MarginMail isn't in that path and never sees your login |

**What's true in every tier:**
- **No MarginMail server.** MarginMail talks to Google directly from your Mac. Its own small settings live in your Google Drive's hidden app folder.
- **No analytics.** We can't see how you use MarginMail.
- **AI never sends.** Write it fills the composer; you read it and press ⌘⏎. Anything the draft added that the thread didn't have (a new recipient, a link, a number or a code) is flagged.
- **Tier 3 is click-only and read-only.** Your Claude runs with MarginMail's read-only tools; it can't send, delete, create filters or fetch the web.
- **Off means off.** Turn AI off in Settings › Intelligence and every rules feature keeps working.

### Who should choose what

- **Want the most powerful AI and don't mind a vendor cloud?** A vendor-cloud app gives you more automation today.
- **Already pay for Gemini or Copilot?** Your provider's AI keeps mail inside the company that already hosts it.
- **Want AI with no third party at all?** Apple Mail's on-device features, or MarginMail's Tier 2, keep it on your device.
- **Want strong AI drafting, but under your own account?** Bring-your-own-model setups like MarginMail's Tier 3 or Missive's API keys.
- **Want no AI?** Mimestream, or MarginMail with AI off.

### FAQ

**What is the most private AI email app for Mac?**
The most private setup has no app-maker server, runs AI on your Mac, and only uses a cloud model you chose, when you ask. MarginMail is built that way for Gmail: rules and Apple Intelligence on your Mac first, your own Claude only on click, and AI never sends.

**Is there an email client that doesn't store my emails on its servers?**
Yes. Some native clients connect directly to your mail provider from your device, with no sync server of their own. For Gmail on the Mac, MarginMail and Mimestream both work this way; MarginMail also runs no analytics and keeps its AI on your Mac or your own Claude.

**Does on-device AI mean my email never leaves my Mac?**
For the on-device part, yes: the model runs locally and nothing is uploaded. MarginMail's Request notes use Apple's on-device model. Apple Mail also uses Private Cloud Compute for some requests. If you opt into a cloud model, like your own Claude, the conversation you send goes to that provider.

**Can I use my own Claude with Gmail?**
Yes, with MarginMail on a Mac. MarginMail finds the Claude Code you installed and uses it, under your own plan, only when you click Write it or What's been decided. It never sees your Claude login and doesn't use an API key.

**Can AI email apps send messages without asking?**
Some can. Several apps let connected agents send mail, sometimes without approving each message. MarginMail's AI can only draft; sending is always your keystroke.
